title: Adaptive blockwise KV quantization sweep and runtime switching (FP8/INT8/INT4)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run an end-to-end experimental sweep of blockwise and layerwise KV cache quantization strategies (dynamic range FP8, symmetric INT8, and aggressive INT4) across representative production traffic to characterize quality degradation, memory savings, and runtime switching costs. The goal is to produce an actionable policy and prototype runtime that can switch quantization encodings per-request or per-model-segment to meet target memory envelopes without exceeding quality budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Quantization sweep completed across 6 representative models and 3 sequence length buckets
Evaluation harness produces per-prompt fidelity metrics (ROUGE-L, embedding drift, token-level perplexity) and a single SLO curve mapping memory savings to quality loss
Prototype runtime supports per-shard blockwise decoding with on-the-fly dequantization and a safe fallback to full-precision KV when quality delta exceeds threshold
Documented heuristics for when to use FP8 vs INT8 vs INT4 for different layers/attention heads
Performance regression < 10% tail latency increase at 95th percentile for typical batch sizes
steps: Design calibration routine for blockwise scale factors and per-layer clipping using calibration corpus
Implement blockwise encoder/decoder for KV shards in the serving runtime with minimal copies
Integrate runtime flagging to dynamically pick quant format per-request based on policy
Run offline sweep with 3 encodings (FP8, INT8 symmetric, INT4 with per-block scale) and compare against baseline FP16/32
Aggregate fidelity metrics and generate memory vs quality trade-off curves
Prototype graceful fallback that triggers when per-request eval metric crosses threshold
results_summary: Preliminary sweep completed on 6 open models and 4 real workload traces. Key findings: FP8 with blockwise per-32 token scaling yields ~1.9x memory reduction vs FP16 with median quality drift <0.8% on embedding similarity and <=1.2 pt ROUGE-L delta on summarization prompts. INT8 symmetric produces similar memory savings but shows higher variance on long-context (>2048) generation traces. INT4 achieves up to 3.6x memory reduction but introduces catastrophic tail regressions on ~3% of prompts; those are highly concentrated in low-entropy instruction-following tasks. Runtime switching overhead is ~3-5ms per request for our hot-path dequantize+KV-merge implementation; this is acceptable for P1 latency targets when amortized across batching. Socialized initial findings with PM/Research; recommended guarded rollout with threshold-based fallbacks and per-customer opt-in for INT4 aggressive mode.
next_steps: Widen sweep to additional customer corpora (PII-handling teams) to validate edge-case regressions
Add per-head sensitivity probe to identify attention heads robust to lower bitwidths
Optimize dequant kernel to reduce runtime switching overhead under continuous batching
Prepare canary plan for dedicated capacity with INT8 default and INT4 experimental flag
Draft RFC for runtime rollout and telemetry signals to monitor quality drift in production
